standard.title: Design and structure media arts works
standard.description: design and structure media arts works to communicate ideas, perspectives and meaning for an intended audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan and structure media arts works with basic pre-production tools (AC9AMA6C01). They have not yet made deliberate design decisions about media languages and technical elements with a clear rationale for how each serves the intended representation for a specific audience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students design and structure media arts works where media language and technical element choices are deliberate and connected to intended ideas, perspectives and meaning for a specific audience.

nodes.label: Planning with pre-production tools
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use pre-production planning tools to design a media arts work with deliberate choices about structure, genre and representational intent
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one pre-production planning tool (storyboard, shooting script, production schedule); explain how at least two design choices communicate intended meaning for the audience
nodes.typical_width: Use appropriate pre-production templates to plan a media arts work; make deliberate choices about structure, genre conventions and media languages; justify each choice in relation to intended meaning and audience
wider: Trial multiple structural approaches using storyboards — evaluate how different structures change what the work communicates and select the most effective
Plan a hybrid production by combining genre conventions — evaluate how the hybrid structure serves the intended meaning in ways single genres cannot
Develop a production schedule that considers responsible media practices throughout — plan how ICIP, copyright and ethical representation obligations will be met

response_modes.reason: Using pre-production tools productively — making deliberate choices and justifying them in relation to intended meaning — is a planning habit that develops through repeated cycles of planning and production. Students who complete planning tools as a formality without genuine deliberation don't develop the pre-production discipline that makes production more intentional.

success_criteria: Uses at least one pre-production planning tool
Explains how at least two design choices communicate intended meaning for the audience
Planning is deliberate — choices are justified, not just listed

nodes.label: Designing representations with media languages
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can design representations using technical and symbolic elements — sound, lighting, framing, colour, font — that serve intended meaning for a specific audience
nodes.minimum_width: Design at least two technical or symbolic elements in a media arts work with a clear reason for how each serves the intended meaning for the audience
nodes.typical_width: Design representations using a range of technical and symbolic elements; explain how each choice constructs intended meaning; consider how choices address issues such as bias, identity or stereotyping
wider: Design representations that deliberately challenge stereotyping, bias or unequal power relationships — evaluate whether the technical and symbolic choices achieve the intended challenge

Experiment with technical and symbolic elements to construct representations that address social issues (identity, sustainability, social justice) — evaluate the effectiveness for the intended audience
Design representations that are safe, legal, ethical and responsible — develop criteria for evaluating own representational choices before production

response_modes.reason: Students commonly design representations using familiar conventions without reasoning about whether those conventions serve the intended meaning or simply reproduce dominant representations. Designing across different representational challenges — identity, power, social issues — forces students to develop deliberate media language design rather than defaulting to genre norms.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Designing representations that deliberately challenge stereotyping and address social issues is genuinely richer than designing conventional narrative media. Advancing students who work in this direction develop critical media literacy alongside production skills — understanding media as a site of ideological work, not just storytelling.
success_criteria: Designs at least two technical or symbolic elements with clear reasons
Explains how each choice constructs meaning for the audience
Design choices go beyond genre convention — connected to specific representational intent

nodes.label: Designing for specific audiences with empathy
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can design media arts works that consider the intended audience relationship and approach representations of characters and cultural content with empathy and responsibility
nodes.minimum_width: Design a media arts work with at least one explicit consideration of the audience relationship; explain how design choices create or shape that relationship
nodes.typical_width: Design media arts works with deliberate attention to audience relationships; apply empathy and respect when designing representations of cultural or social groups; document reasoning
wider: Design characters or representations that convey historical or cultural ideas with genuine empathy — evaluate whether design choices honour the people or cultures represented
Plan how to create relationships with audiences when developing characters — investigate how different design approaches create different emotional and cognitive responses
Design a work that explores how people are engaging in online social justice campaigns — evaluate how design choices can build solidarity or reinforce distance with the intended audience

response_modes.reason: Students commonly design for an abstract 'audience' without reasoning through who the specific audience is, what relationship the work should create with them, and how design choices build or undermine that relationship. Scaffolding the audience design reasoning — who are they, what do I want them to feel/think/do, which design choices serve that — builds audience-centred design thinking.

This node integrates pre-production planning (Node 1), deliberate media language design (Node 2), and investigative work from E01/E02 into a coherent design that serves a specific audience with appropriate ethical responsibility. Students who can design technically but cannot reason through the audience relationship and representational ethics have not met the standard's full demand.

success_criteria: Designs with at least one explicit consideration of the audience relationship
Explains how design choices create that relationship
Representations of cultural or social groups demonstrate empathy and responsibility
